questions.question: Q: What is image stacking and why is it used?
questions.correctAnswer: Combining multiple short exposures of the same object to reduce random noise and increase signal-to-noise ratio, revealing fainter detail than a single long exposure.

questions.question: Q: What are dark frames and flat frames?
questions.correctAnswer: Dark frames: exposures with the lens cap on, recording sensor noise for subtraction. Flat frames: images of a uniform light source, correcting vignetting and dust shadows on the sensor.

questions.question: Q: How are star trail images created?
questions.correctAnswer: By taking a very long exposure (or stacking many short ones) while the camera remains fixed, recording the apparent circular motion of stars around the celestial pole.

questions.question: Q: What is the '500 rule' in astrophotography?
questions.correctAnswer: A guide for maximum exposure time without star trailing on a fixed tripod: 500 ÷ focal length (mm) = max seconds. E.g. with a 50mm lens: 500/50 = 10 seconds.

questions.question: Q: Why is a tracking mount needed for deep-sky imaging?
questions.correctAnswer: Deep-sky objects are very faint and require long total exposure times. A tracking mount follows the sky's rotation, keeping stars pin-point rather than trailing.
